title: Dedicated capacity containment ops and root cause investigation for unexpected throughput shortfall
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Production dedicated pools in us-west experienced a sustained throughput shortfall starting 2026-02-25 02:10 UTC. Token throughput dropped ~40% for affected tenants and queue depth increased for 18 minutes. This ticket tracks containment, root-cause analysis, and post-incident mitigations.

Observed behavior: SLO alert fired on 99th percentile latency and queue-growth. Autoscaler initiated scale-downs starting 02:12 UTC based on node CPU signals; within 5 minutes pod churn increased and healthy capacity fell further. A manual rollback of the scheduler binary to the previous release restored steady-state capacity at 02:34 UTC.

Why this matters: Dedicated customers experienced degraded performance and increased errors during the window. Because autoscaler interpreted short-lived signals as lower demand, the system entered a feedback loop that amplified the outage.

Immediate containment: shift traffic off impacted pools using weighted routing, enable emergency-hedge capacity (reserve hot-spare nodes), and temporarily disable aggressive scale-down policy for all dedicated pools until the autoscaler policy is patched.
root_cause_summary: Root cause is a combination of three factors: (1) a scheduler labeling regression in orchestrator v4.2 that caused new allocation units to be scheduled onto node classes with an incorrect preemption profile; (2) a change in kernel selection heuristics that altered process-level CPU accounting reported by node exporter, resulting in underreported CPU utilization; (3) an autoscaler policy that treats transient decreases in reported node CPU as sustained low demand and aggressively scales down without considering recent eviction churn. These factors combined to create a feedback loop: churn -> lower reported CPU -> scale-down -> reduced capacity -> more churn.

comments: 2026-02-25 02:25 - Ravi Patel: Taking command. Initiated traffic-weight shift to reserve pools and disabled aggressive downscale flag for dedicated autoscaler. Gathering logs and correlated deployments.
2026-02-25 02:36 - Maya Chen: Confirmed rollback of orchestrator scheduler to v4.1 restored expected allocation behavior. Continuing to validate across tenants.

2026-02-26 11:12 - Lucia Ramos (SRE): We observed node-exporter v3.7 reported 30-40% lower cgroup cpu usage for processes after the kernel heuristics change. Instrumentation added to surface raw cgroup counters in metrics pipeline.

2026-02-27 15:05 - Ravi Patel: Hotfix for autoscaler merged (PR #4678). Changes: add eviction-aware downscale cooldown, require moving-average window of 5m with min-samples check, and tie decision to queue latency metric in addition to node CPU.
